name: Pride and Prejudice
shortDescription: Jane Austen's classic novel of manners, marriage, and wit.
longDescription: Set in Georgian England, Pride and Prejudice follows Elizabeth Bennet as she navigates issues of manners, upbringing, morality, and marriage in the landed gentry society of early 19th-century England. Its wit and social commentary have made it one of the most beloved novels in English literature.

shortDescription: George Orwell's dystopian vision of a totalitarian future.
longDescription: In a world of perpetual war, omnipresent surveillance, and constant public manipulation, 1984 follows Winston Smith's struggle against Big Brother's regime. Orwell's chilling vision remains a defining work of 20th-century fiction.

name: The Great Gatsby
shortDescription: F. Scott Fitzgerald's portrait of the Jazz Age and the American Dream.
longDescription: Narrated by Nick Carraway, The Great Gatsby explores themes of decadence, idealism, resistance to change, and excess through the mysterious millionaire Jay Gatsby and his obsession with Daisy Buchanan.

name: Moby Dick
shortDescription: Herman Melville's epic tale of obsession at sea.
longDescription: Moby Dick follows the voyage of the whaling ship Pequod, commanded by Captain Ahab, who leads a monomaniacal quest to kill the white whale that took his leg. A sprawling meditation on fate, obsession, and nature.

reviews.comment: Long, but the whaling chapters are fascinating.

name: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
shortDescription: Yuval Noah Harari's sweeping history of the human species.
longDescription: Sapiens surveys the history of humankind from the emergence of Homo sapiens in Africa to the political and technological revolutions of today, exploring how biology and history have defined us.

name: Thinking, Fast and Slow
shortDescription: Daniel Kahneman's landmark exploration of the two systems that drive our thinking.
longDescription: Kahneman, winner of the Nobel Prize in Economics, explains the two systems that drive the way we think: System 1, fast and intuitive, and System 2, slower and more deliberate, revealing the biases baked into our judgment.

name: Educated
shortDescription: Tara Westover's memoir of self-invention through education.
longDescription: Educated is the story of a woman who grows up in a survivalist family in rural Idaho and, without ever setting foot in a classroom, goes on to earn a PhD from Cambridge University.

name: A Brief History of Time
shortDescription: Stephen Hawking's classic introduction to cosmology.
longDescription: Stephen Hawking explains the origin and fate of the universe, from the Big Bang to black holes, making complex cosmology accessible to a general audience.

name: Clean Code
shortDescription: Robert C. Martin's guide to writing maintainable software.
longDescription: Clean Code presents a comprehensive framework of best practices, principles, and heuristics for writing readable, maintainable code, with case studies of cleaning up bad code.

reviews.comment: Dated examples but the principles hold up.

name: The Pragmatic Programmer
shortDescription: Hunt and Thomas's timeless guide to software craftsmanship.
longDescription: The Pragmatic Programmer covers topics ranging from personal responsibility and career development to architectural techniques for keeping code flexible and easy to adapt and reuse.

name: Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software
shortDescription: The Gang of Four's foundational catalog of software design patterns.
longDescription: This book introduces 23 classic design patterns for object-oriented software design, providing a shared vocabulary for solving recurring design problems.

name: Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code
shortDescription: Martin Fowler's catalog of techniques for improving code without changing behavior.
longDescription: Refactoring provides a catalog of proven techniques for improving the design of existing code, teaching developers how to recognize code smells and fix them incrementally.

reviews.comment: The refactoring catalog alone is worth it.

name: The Lean Startup
shortDescription: Eric Ries's method for building successful startups through validated learning.
longDescription: The Lean Startup introduces a scientific approach to creating and managing startups, using validated learning, rapid experimentation, and iterative product releases to shorten development cycles.

reviews.comment: Reshaped how I think about MVPs.

name: Good to Great
shortDescription: Jim Collins's research into what makes companies achieve lasting greatness.
longDescription: Good to Great presents the findings of a five-year research project identifying the factors that allowed some companies to make the leap from good performance to great, sustained results.

name: Zero to One
shortDescription: Peter Thiel's notes on startups and building the future.
longDescription: Zero to One presents Peter Thiel's unconventional thinking on how to build companies that create new things, moving the world from 0 to 1 rather than copying existing ideas.

name: The Innovator's Dilemma
shortDescription: Clayton Christensen's theory of disruptive innovation.
longDescription: The Innovator's Dilemma explains why successful companies can fail by doing everything 'right,' and introduces the theory of disruptive technologies that reshape entire industries.

name: Atomic Habits
shortDescription: James Clear's practical guide to building good habits.
longDescription: Atomic Habits offers a proven framework for improving every day, showing how tiny changes can deliver remarkable results through the compounding of small habits.

name: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
shortDescription: Stephen Covey's classic framework for personal and professional effectiveness.
longDescription: The 7 Habits presents a principle-centered approach to solving personal and professional problems, built around habits like being proactive and beginning with the end in mind.

reviews.comment: A foundational read, still holds up.

name: Mindset: The New Psychology of Success
shortDescription: Carol Dweck's research on the power of the growth mindset.
longDescription: Mindset reveals how the view we adopt for ourselves profoundly affects the way we lead our lives, distinguishing between a 'fixed' and a 'growth' mindset and how each shapes success.

name: Deep Work
shortDescription: Cal Newport's argument for focused success in a distracted world.
longDescription: Deep Work argues that the ability to focus without distraction is becoming increasingly rare and valuable, and provides a rigorous training regimen for cultivating a deep work habit.

reviews.comment: Directly improved my focus at work.
